evidence.title: Related Digital, Blackstone, Oracle, OpenAI, Walbridge and Governor Whitmer celebrate construction of Stargate campus in Saline Township
evidence.excerpt: The Saline Township Stargate campus is under construction, with all three data-center buildings actively under construction.

metadata.content_hash_scope: SHA-256 of retrieved HTML response bytes
metadata.coordinate_basis: Approximate Saline Township project point rounded from public locality context; not a parcel or building coordinate.
metadata.status_scope: The developer says the campus is under construction, all campus buildings are actively under construction, and the first of three buildings is nearing completion.
metadata.physical_scope: The source describes three 550,000-square-foot single-story data-center buildings on a 250-acre campus.
metadata.cooling_statement: The source describes a closed-loop, air-cooled system and does not provide PUE.
metadata.roles_guardrail: Related Digital is the developer, Walbridge is the contractor, and the campus is being delivered for Oracle and OpenAI; the source does not establish a separate landlord or final operating-entity record.
metadata.capacity_guardrail: The construction source does not type its gigawatt-scale wording. The separate DTE utility disclosure supports only a contracted grid-load observation.

evidence.title: DTE Energy reports 2025 accomplishments, earnings and investments
evidence.excerpt: DTE says approved hyperscale contracts provide 1.4 GW of electric load for Oracle's Saline Township data center.

metadata.content_hash_scope: SHA-256 of retrieved HTML response bytes
metadata.metric_scope: DTE explicitly describes 1.4 gigawatts of load in approved hyperscale data-center contracts for the Saline Township project.
metadata.metric_typing: Imported as contracted grid_connection_mw because the utility describes contracted electric service/load; not critical IT load, gross facility load, generation nameplate, PUE, or measured annual energy.
metadata.annual_energy_method: The forecast annual-energy interval is an Atlas model from contracted grid load: zero downside for delay or curtailment, 80 percent load factor at base, and 100 percent at high, each over 8,760 hours.
metadata.annual_energy_guardrail: The annual-energy observation is modeled, not metered or company-reported consumption.
